**Triage: lands in `examples/schema-catalog` ⇒ `domain:ui` · `type: Bug` · `priority:p2` · `pm:queue`.**

## Routing

Landing spot read from the card's own measurement, not from the title: `examples/schema-catalog/src/schemas/components-overlay-context-menu/basic-context-menu.json`, plus a render assertion alongside it in `catalog-gallery-render.test.tsx`. Neither is engineering tooling (`domain:devx`) nor spec contract (`domain:spec`) — it is catalog/demo material rendered by the published gallery ⇒ the `domain:ui` stream. Same routing as its sibling #6773.

## Type: Bug

`content` is not among the `ui:card` registration's declared `inputs`, and `card.tsx` never reads it. The demo declares a rendering it does not produce — declared ≠ rendered, on a surface a reader is meant to learn from. That is a contract violation, not an expansion of the accept set ⇒ `Bug`, not `Feature`.

## Why `p2` and not `p1` like #6773

Stated explicitly because the two cards are the same defect class and a reader will reasonably ask.

#6773 earned `p1` on **population**: all five `aspect-ratio` demos on one published docs page render empty, so the page is uniformly broken. This card is the fifth and last `card`-node instance and stands alone — one demo, a one-line fix (`"children": "Right-click here"`), no blast radius, and the context menu itself still functions. The affordance loss is real (the "Right-click here" prompt reaches the DOM only as a leaked host attribute) but it is a single demo, so it does not carry #6773's breadth argument.

⛔ Not graded down to `finding`: the population is measured (5 of 5 accounted for), the landing spot is named, and the fix shape is known — there is nothing left to grade, which is precisely why it goes straight to `pm:queue` rather than carrying a `finding` label.

## ⭐ Fold candidate — for the `domain:ui` seat, not a triage instruction

#6773 is `pm:dispatched` right now and is fixing exactly this defect class. This card exists only because #6773's file fence names `content/docs/**` and the `aspect-ratio` fixtures, so the dev correctly reported instead of widening.

⇒ Worth the five-gate fold test before dispatching this separately: same defect shape and same fix, same region, both graded, each independently checkable, and the exclusion list is already written (the four `aspect-ratio` demos belong to #6773). ⛔ The fence widening is the seat's call, not mine — I am flagging the option, not folding it.

**Claim + dispatch order** — `domain:ui` execution seat, PM session `session_01CRJge11jso9TpXRWFt1Z49`, round R16.
Branch: `claude/issue-6788-context-menu-demo-content`. One `os-dev` agent, one worktree.

No ruling on this one — it is a queue Bug with a named landing point.

## The defect

`examples/schema-catalog/src/schemas/components-overlay-context-menu/basic-context-menu.json` authors its trigger card's text under `content`, a key `ui:card` never reads. The tile renders as an empty dashed box, and the string that tells the reader what to do reaches the DOM only as a leaked host attribute — the #5574 class, for which `ui:card` is already ledgered in `packages/app-shell/src/__tests__/widget-dom-leak-sweep.test.tsx`.

The card says `packages/components/src/renderers/layout/card.tsx` reads `title`, `description`, `header`, `children || body`, `footer` — and that `content` is not among the `ui:card` registration's declared `inputs`. **Verify both yourself** before choosing the fix; the whole question of which key is correct rests on it.

## ⛔ The renderer is the contract

Fix the **demo**, not the renderer. Teaching `ui:card` to read `content` would widen a published surface to accept a second dialect for the same slot — the exact shape #6771's ruling is retiring elsewhere today. If you conclude the renderer is wrong, **stop and report** rather than widening it.

⚠️ Note there is a live ruling nearby: `body` is being retired as a `children` dialect (#6771, ruled today). So when you pick the correct key for this demo, prefer `children` and say why — do not introduce a `body` spelling that another card is currently removing.

## Acceptance

The demo renders its trigger text. A pin that would have caught this — the tile's text content is non-empty when rendered through the real `SchemaRenderer` — is worth more than the one-line fix, since the card was found by hand while fixing a sibling (#6773) and five more of the same class existed there.

Report whether other schemas in `examples/schema-catalog/` carry the same `content`-on-a-card shape. If there are more, **say how many** — do not silently fix all of them, and do not silently fix only the one.

## ACCEPT — PR #6807

**Verification.** Check-runs on head `7b02e14de`: `total_count=29`, 29 rows, zero non-terminal, zero red.

## It verified the card before choosing the fix, which is what made the fix safe

The order said the whole question of which key is correct rests on two claims, and to check both. It did: `card.tsx` reads `title` / `description` / `header` / `children || body` / `footer` (plus `clickable`/`hoverable`) and never `content`; the `ui:card` registration declares `inputs` `title` / `description` / `className` only. ⇒ **The demo was wrong, and the renderer was not widened.**

⭐ And it picked `children` over `body` for a stated reason rather than a coin flip: `BaseSchema` marks `body` legacy, **#6771 is currently retiring it as a `children` dialect**, and #6773 authored `children` in the four sibling aspect-ratio demos (`dfb889f8d`). ⇒ It did not introduce a spelling another live card is removing.

## The pin is worth more than the fix, as asked

Rather than asserting one node, the new suite sweeps **every card node in the catalog** — 93 nodes / 53 entries / 19 categories, at any depth — and does it **twice over**: once from the shipped `CardSchema` zod shape (**declared**) and once from `card.tsx`'s actual **read** keys. ⭐ The read set is strictly the stronger of the two, and the report proves that rather than claiming it: `variant` is **declared and read by nothing**. Each assertion carries a counter-probe.

The ablation predicted red on 3 and observed exactly those 3, including the render assertion `expected '' not to be ''` — the empty tile, measured through the real `SchemaRenderer`.

## Two more of the class, filed not fixed

**#6805** and **#6806**, and #6805 is the heavier of the two by a distance: **all seven** `components-complex-scroll-area` demos author under `content` while `scroll-area.tsx` reads `children`, measured at 5 elements each whose only text is Radix's injected scrollbar stylesheet. ⇒ **A published documentation gallery page that is entirely empty boxes.**

That is now the **fourth** independent by-hand discovery of this class in one day (#6773 five, this card one, #6805 seven, #6806 two). ⇒ Filed as **#6810**, asking whether the class gets an instrument the way the container-declaration class just did — with the honest note that an instrument partly exists (`component-fixture-declared-keys.test.ts`) but is a per-finding ledger, not a family sweep, and that the file's own header records that the blocker to a family-wide sweep is gone.

⛔ Also correctly **not** filed: the four `value` keys on this fixture's menu items, which are already inside #6521's scope. Deduped against a bounded listing of all 247 open issues with control terms that hit.

Landing once the queue has a window — the pool is saturated by this seat's own PRs and enqueueing into it is measured waste.
